about: Antonio Vallana e Figlio was founded in 1937 in Maggiora, in the Novara hills of Alto Piemonte, about 100 miles northeast of Barolo. In the late 1950s and 1960s Antonio’s son Bernardo made Spanna, the local name for Nebbiolo, that was compared with the great Barolos of Giacomo Conterno and Bartolo Mascarello and was collected by New York wine lovers. Today Bernardo’s grandchildren, Marina and Francis Fogarty, make the wines by his traditional methods and have been reclaiming the family’s old vineyards in Boca, the source of the estate’s celebrated Montalbano and Traversagna bottlings of the 1950s and 60s.

Boca is one of Alto Piemonte’s small hill appellations, set at the foot of the Alps, where cool mountain air, nearby lakes and ancient volcanic soils give Nebbiolo a fresh, mineral edge. Vallana’s 2018 blends Nebbiolo with the local Vespolina and Uva Rara. Each grape is picked by hand and fermented separately in old cement vats, then the blend ages for about two years in large 10-hectolitre casks. Boca must age at least four years before release. Vinous called the 2018 an old-school, classic Boca, with firm tannins around a core of dark cherry, and recommended decanting it. Look too for cedar, plum, orange zest and thyme.
